summary: This bill amends title 18 of the U.S. Code to make it a federal crime, punishable by up to 18 years in prison, for a registered sex offender to use interstate commerce to enter a surrogacy arrangement with intent to exercise parental rights over the child, or for any person entering such an arrangement who commits a sex offense before the child's birth.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations of any kind.
The bill makes no changes to tax law, rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
While surrogacy involves reproductive processes, the bill is a narrow criminal prohibition targeting sex offenders and does not alter healthcare policy, coverage, or regulation.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not affect immigration law, visas, borders, or pathways to citizenship.
The legislation restricts surrogacy for sex offenders but contains no language regarding abortion access, procedures, or restrictions.
No references to military, defense spending, or national security appropriations.
The bill has no environmental, regulatory, or climate-related content.
No provisions impact welfare programs, food assistance, or social services.
The bill does not address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No content related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.

The bill adds new federal criminal offenses under title 18, prohibiting registered sex offenders from entering surrogacy arrangements via interstate commerce and imposing penalties of fines or up to 18 years imprisonment. This expands criminal prohibitions and applies stricter enforcement measures specifically targeting sex offenders.
No provisions on tariffs, trade agreements, or protectionism.
The bill has no fiscal impact or implications for deficits or debt reduction.
Although surrogacy can involve diverse family structures, the bill's prohibition is limited to sex offenders and does not expand or restrict LGBTQ+ legal protections.
No references to foreign assistance or international aid programs.
The bill does not address voting rights, election procedures, or voter integrity measures.
Mentions of 'instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce' are incidental to defining the crime and do not regulate technology, data, or privacy.
No content related to workers' rights, unions, or employment regulations.
The bill contains no provisions on religious exemptions or civil rights protections.
